notes: This page continues with application. and ends after the lower drawing. No date or dark authorial page number is visible. The separate pale lower-left 96 is preserved as a margin item, without attributing that foliation to the author.

The original and the two native-resolution halves were inspected once each, line by line. Twelve distinct local crops were created once from the original, with original coordinates recorded on their associated changes/decisions. All twelve crops were visually inspected. They were enlarged by LANCZOS to 2800 pixels wide, except the folio crop at 2400, with autocontrast and mild sharpening; no rotation was applied.

The source describes an involution that is no longer required to have no fixed points. It identifies I with the fixed-point set and calls the corresponding features branches aplaties and pts-bord outside S. These are statements transcribed from this page, not independently proved here.

The source then describes the data as an ordinary graph together with an ensemble I and an application I→S. The interlinear tuple belongs after graphe ordinaire, as shown by its curved leader. H’s placement before d’un is not retained.

The opening involution index and the complement operand remain unresolved from the actual retraced strokes. Both full formulas were checked locally. No mathematical expectation has removed either doubt, and no underlying overwritten character has been invented as a separate deletion.

All four occurrences of aplaties were separately resolved on their own inspected crops. The noun branches was also checked at every occurrence against H’s boucles, including the tall h and compressed r/an strokes.

The upper graph has five solid dots and six free ends: two at the upper-left dot, three at the lower-left dot, and one at the central dot. Two edges connect the central dot with the next dot to its right; a single edge reaches the final looped dot. These are visual counts of the source drawing.

The lower drawing has three open-centred ink circles at the central, middle and right loop-junction positions. The ends labelled 2 and 3 are thick hooks, not corresponding circles. The transcription preserves that visible distinction and makes no claim about whether those ends should mathematically be counted as vertices. The labels are exactly 1 above the central circle, 2 above the upper-left end, and 3 beside the lower-left end.

The pale folio omission, both drawing discrepancies, actual lexical differences, and insertion placements are collated. H’s editorial sentence La phrase s’interrompt après le dessin is treated as a drawing-description comment, not as authorial words or an extra source-text error. Plain macro substitutions and dash macro choices are not counted.

Four cancellations and four insertions are represented. The raised 1- prefix is the insertion state missing from C. The cancellations bouts and couple retain local uncertainty; sont remains readable through its strokes, while blind review leaves se/de locally doubtful. Commas and the live quoted pts-bord remain outside the preceding cancellations.

The main reader reported direct inspection of the original, all twelve crops and the complete TeX draft, concurring with the local readings and retained uncertainties. No proof check or external source was used, and no TeX compilation was performed.

Blind audit confirms branches in all four occurrences, the ordinary-graph tuple with o, and the two drawings. The lower drawing retains three open-centred junctions and two hooked left tips, which the blind draft had represented as filled circles. The opening pair of quotation ticks before gros is added without inventing a closing pair. The old se/de is left doubtful under its strike.
